draft.title: Decolonisation
card: Decolonisation is the process by which colonies gained independence from the European powers that ruled them. Many colonies in Asia and Africa won it after 1945.
The Second World War weakened Britain, France and the Netherlands. Many colonised peoples had also come to expect self-rule, and nationalist movements grew stronger.
the colonial power agreed to leave through talks and a set date. India and Pakistan became independent from Britain in 1947, and Ghana did so in 1957.
the colonial power resisted, and independence came after armed conflict. Indonesia fought the Dutch from 1945 to 1949, and Algeria fought France from 1954 to 1962.
draft.remember: Colonies won independence after 1945, by agreement in some cases and by war in others.

opts: Colonies gaining independence from the powers that ruled
Colonial powers taking over new land in Asia and Africa
Colonies agreeing to be ruled by a neighbouring country
Colonial powers moving their people into their colonies
a.why: Decolonisation means a colony gaining independence from the power that ruled it. Taking over new land is the reverse, which is colonisation.
a.clue: Think about who ends up in control of the colony.

b.q: In 1954 fighters in Algeria began an armed struggle against France, which refused to leave. Independence came in 1962. What does this case show about decolonisation?
opts: It could come through war when the ruler resisted
It always came through war once nationalists organised
It could only come once the ruler agreed to leave
It came only to colonies that were not ruled by France
b.why: France resisted and independence followed armed conflict, so decolonisation could come through war. It did not always do so, because India and Ghana gained independence through talks with Britain.

a.best: Colonies gaining independence from the powers that ruled

b.best: It could come through war when the ruler resisted

problems.detail: India and Pakistan are given as the example of a 'peaceful transfer' with no mention that partition in 1947 brought mass violence, with hundreds of thousands killed and millions displaced. The handover from Britain was negotiated, but students could come away thinking Indian independence was peaceful overall. A short qualifier such as 'the handover was agreed, though partition was violent' would fix this.
The remember line says 'Colonies won independence after 1945', dropping the card's 'Many colonies'. This implies that all colonies did, which the card does not claim.
The option 'Colonies gaining independence from the powers that ruled' is missing its object ('ruled them'), so it reads as an incomplete phrase.
